mechanism_narrative: The sustained and accelerating upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a strong underlying momentum for increased out-of-home activity, which will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks as consumer confidence builds.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The return of GROCERY_PHARM mobility to pre-baseline levels (0% change) signifies a broad comfort among the population with essential public outings. This increased comfort will quickly translate into higher discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 14 days following GROCERY_PHARM crossing 0%, suggesting the comfort level does not extend to discretionary spending.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility and increase in PARKS mobility indicates a strong behavioral shift towards spending more time outside the home and engaging in leisure activities. This combined trend will drive a significant increase in RETAIL_REC as people seek more diverse out-of-home experiences over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to fall and PARKS continuing to rise, indicating a decoupling of leisure behavior from retail.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and significant recovery in TRANSIT station mobility suggests a policy-driven or encouraged return to public transport and urban centers. This increased movement of people through transit hubs will directly lead to higher foot traffic and spending in retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show an increase, despite TRANSIT mobility continuing its upward trend, suggesting public transport usage is not translating to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility signals a renewed return to office environments. This influx of workers will immediately boost local retail and recreation activity during weekdays, leading to higher RETAIL_REC in the very short term (next week).
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 7 days following a week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES of more than 5 points, indicating no immediate spillover effect.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained four-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a fundamental shift in daily routines, with people spending progressively less time at home. This persistent trend implies a greater propensity for out-of-home activities, which will directly translate to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing its downward trend, suggesting a shift to other non-retail out-of-home activities.

mechanism_narrative: The combined strong and consistent increase in PARKS and TRANSIT mobility, occurring in mid-February, suggests an early seasonal uplift in outdoor activity and public movement, likely driven by improving weather. This seasonal shift will encourage more general out-of-home activity, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 14 days, despite PARKS and TRANSIT continuing to rise, indicating that seasonal factors are not translating to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility fails to show a sustained recovery and instead stagnates or declines over the next two weeks, it signals a lack of confidence in returning to normal work routines. This stagnation in economic activity will depress overall consumer spending and lead to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls or changes by less than 1 point for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES mobility remaining flat or declining, suggesting other factors are driving retail recovery.
